summary: Wire enter, stay and exit responses on a 3D trigger in the Inspector, with a tag filter.
overview: Drop it on a trigger collider and wire the responses — no code for a "when the player enters this zone, do X" setup. The 2D counterpart is a separate component because Unity's 2D and 3D physics callbacks are different methods entirely.
useCases: Checkpoints, door triggers and zone transitions.
Triggering a cutscene or spawning a wave on entry.

params.tuning: Untagged means everything matches, which is rarely what a zone wants.
Off ignores the tag entirely and fires for every collider, including projectiles and debris.

gotchas.title: It needs a trigger collider and, usually, a rigidbody
gotchas.body: Unity only raises trigger callbacks when at least one of the two objects has a Rigidbody. A static trigger and a static mover never fire.

gotchas.title: Stay fires every physics step
gotchas.body: Anything expensive wired to OnStay runs at the fixed timestep rate, not once.
